recipes.name: Easy Homemade Pie Crust
ingredients_raw: 1 cup unsalted butter - chilled, cut into tablespoon-size pieces

steps.text: Combine flour, butter, and salt in a food processor. Pulse until mixture resembles coarse crumbs, about 10 (1-second) pulses.
Stir ice water and vinegar in a small bowl.

Pour 1/2 of the ice water mixture into flour mixture; pulse to combine, about 3 (1-second) pulses. Pour in remaining ice water mixture; pulse until mixture starts to come together, about 8 (1-second) pulses.
Turn dough out onto a wooden surface, pat it into a circle, and divide it in half. Form each half into a disc, about 5-inches wide.
Wrap each disc in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes until ready to use.
Use in your favorite pie recipe.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Homemade Pie Crust
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's pie crust recipe comes together quickly in a food processor and chills into two buttery, flaky discs—perfect for sweet or savory pies.

review.reviewBody: This is my 1st attempt on making a pie crust from scratch.. so I followed everything exactly and was kinda nervous at first but it came out really well! Flaky and really light! Chef John never fails to impress! Oh and I had some dough left for half a crust, lolz..

So like the negative reviews say, yes, this crust can be quite hard when baked and tricky to work with because it's so crumbly. What I do is add more water than the recipe calls for, and substitute ¼ of the butter with lard. I also add 2 tablespoons of brown sugar. This makes it pliable, delicious, and much more forgiving. The added water keeps the dough together (you could also try vodka so it evaporates faster while baking), because as it's written it's just too crumbly. That's why the dough bakes hard, you're forced to overwork it trying to get it to become a cohesive dough instead of greasy sand grains. Like all pie doughs it can smell fear and hates being touched. Just let it rest on the counter for ½ hour or so to come back to temp cuz trying to roll butter based pie dough straight from the fridge is like trying to get my ex husband to communicate: difficult and rage-inducing. Overall it's delicious and when done right is very flaky. It just needs a little extra touch to be perfect.

I followed the recipe to a T and it came out too crumbly, not like in the photos. I live on the Canadian prairies. I think our "all purpose flour" is harder than in the U.S. Also the climate is very dry. When I make pie crust with lard I add much more water than the recipe says. A lady who makes pies for the farmers' market told me "You'll think you've got it too wet." but after an hour in the fridge it is perfect. I'll try this next time I make this pie crust, and use 10 tbs. water rather than 7. Incidentally, I've wondered why, on the packet of "all purpose flour" they don't indicate what kind of wheat they are using. All purpose flour isn't the same in different parts of the continent.
Everything was so perfect I did not use a processor I used a pastry cutter and some arm work but came out perfect!
Followed recipe exactly however after cutting up my butter I put it in the freezer for an hour or so. Best pie crust I’ve ever made!

I doubled this recipe and it turned out extremely well. The piecrust was very flaky, even with a wet filling, like a pumpkin pie. I did use approximately 1 cup of that 5 cups of flour though for when I rolled out the dough so it didn’t end up drying out the dough.I also used 1 1/2 cups of Crisco shortening butter flavored and then I used 1/2 butter.

This is by far my favourite pie recipe, I get compliments on this pie crust all the time. It’s good as is, sometimes I’ll add 1/4 cup of white sugar just to sweeten it up but honestly it does not need it. I don’t have a food processor so I lightly stir everything with my hands once it comes together I separate into two balls and put them in the fridge. This recipe is also good to make ahead of time and freeze a few dough balls and thaw once your ready to use them.

This was my first time making homemade pie crust. I haven't had many store bought or homemade pies so I was pretty nervous on how it would turn out. However, I think it was delicious and I received positive feedback as well! It went so well with this apple pie recipe I had.

Since I had a small food processor, I split the recipe and repeated the processing step twice. I also might have to add more water next time because the dough kept breaking around the edges.

Thank you for the recipe! I never thought I'd be making my own pie crust. Now I feel a little inspired to try other pies and designs.

Made it by hand because I can't be bothered to wash my food processor. The vinegar really does make this crust soft. Also made with half butter, half margarine to cut back on the costs. I will definitely make it again.

This is the recipe my 95 year old mother uses! You cannot over work this us dough. It is flakey and delicious every time. You can even freeze it! You don't need a food processor. Just a little gumption! It does not have any vinegar taste...DELICIOUS!
I rolled it out then cut into disks & made hand pies with the dough.

This pie crust recipe is easy, fast, consistent & delicious. Absolute go to for pies & quiches. Perfect to make batches ahead & freeze. Even pleasantly surprised us as a pizza crust when we accidentally forgot to label. Will make an effort to try as calzone crust.
Easy, light and flaky crust! Thanks!
I like how this recipe uses a food processor to cut butter into flour. It is so easy and gives a very flaky crust. Never using store bought crust again

This is the easiest and BEST all-butter pie crust. I've been making excellent pie crusts (according to family and friends) for over 20 years, but it was a chore because I did everything by hand, including cutting in the butter. At first I was skeptical about using a food processor. Thoughts of hard, flat store-bought pies came to mind, but this recipe and Chef John's recipe turned out great the first time and consistently ever since. I'll never go back!
Add a little extra water
The only one I will ever use again!
I could never make home made pie crust until I tried this recipe and now use exclusively.

My first time making pie dough using butter, having only used Crisco previously. Added a bit of sugar as this was for a blueberry basil pie. Very cold ingredients were mixed in the food processor and came together almost immediately. After minimal kneading, the dough was smooth and divided into two flat rounds, wrapped in SaranWrap, then refrigerated overnight along with the pie dish. The cold dough rolled out with little effort. Only minimal bench flour was needed; the dough released from the counter easily . Before putting in the dough, I did lightly spray the dish with Baker’s Joy. The pie was a success. Thank you for an excellent recipe and tutorial.
Did great. Easy too. I hate making crust but this was definitely better than the store bought.
